ideas.name: Ranked: All of Them (working: 'The Complete Atlas')
ideas.oneLiner: Completionist geography mega-guides that rank an entire closed set — all 63 US national parks, every Caribbean island, all 20 regions of Italy — using a transparent on-screen scoring system built from public data, so it's the last video a planner needs.
ideas.format: Exhaustive ranked mega-video, 40-70 min (one segment per item), narrated over public-domain photography and maps, 1/week (heavier builds)
ideas.titleTemplate: "All/Every [N] [complete named set] Ranked, [criterion] ([year])" — e.g. "All 63 US National Parks Ranked Worst to Best (2026)". Sets are endless closed lists: national parks, US states, EU/European countries, Caribbean/Greek/Hawaiian islands, Italian regions, UNESCO sites by region, scenic byways, national monuments — 30+ sets x re-rankable criteria (cost, crowds, road trips, first-timers) = 100+ titles, refreshable annually.

ideas.ownableReframe: Ports the completionist-guide moat from game guides to real-world geography: a closed set, ranked on five public metrics scored live on screen — methodology-as-content turns commodity destination info into an authored, argue-with-able verdict.
ideas.productionModel: Solo, ~18-24 hrs/video but formulaic per segment: NPS photo/video library is public domain (decisive asset win for park sets); USGS/NOAA imagery public domain; Wikimedia Commons CC and Pexels/Mixkit free-license drone b-roll for international sets (license-check per clip); ranking data from public sources (NPS visitation statistics, cost indices from national statistics offices, flight-connectivity data); maps in QGIS/Natural Earth; scorecard graphics templated in After Effects. Policy note: highly templated segments at scale are the exact 'inauthentic content' pattern-match — the on-screen scoring methodology, per-item authored commentary, and varied structure between sets are the required author-input defense.
ideas.whyNow: Exhaustive-ranking demand is visibly live: 'all 63 national parks ranked' returns multiple YouTube videos plus a 2026-maintained ranking site, and reaction videos to a ranking exist (a second-order demand signal) — all Tier B, titles only, view counts unverified. US-heavy subjects skew the audience tier-1, which is the biggest RPM lever per rpm-travel.md. Engine B is proven by Recommended Playing (search-matched exhaustive promise) — with its subscriber-conversion weakness (W5) treated as a known risk, not a surprise.
searchProbes: every european country ranked for travel
risks: W5 head-on: the reference for this model (Recommended Playing) converted search traffic to subs poorly (0.68x) and retired — channel growth may lag revenue; must pair with browse-friendly criteria variants ('quietest', 'overrated')
Highest per-video production weight of the four; 2/week likely impossible, so the volume-lottery variance buffer (W6) is thinner
Inauthentic-content pattern-match risk is highest here (many near-identical segments at scale) — the methodology/commentary defense must be real, not cosmetic
Established competitors own the head term (More Than Just Parks in national parks) — attainability audit downstream is decisive
